title: Warm-up: gentle finger stretches
description: Loosen the hand before exercising. Slow, gentle movements only.
steps: Sit with your forearm resting on a table, palm down.
Spread all fingers apart slowly, hold 3 seconds.
Bring the fingers back together, hold 3 seconds.
Gently shake out the hand for 10 seconds.
Repeat 5 times.
tips: Warm water (not hot) for a few minutes before exercising can make the fingers feel less stiff.

title: Finger flexion: make a soft fist
description: The basic bending exercise measured by the flex sensor on the middle finger.
steps: Start with the hand open and fingers straight.
Slowly bend all fingers toward the palm, as far as is comfortable.
Hold the bent position for 2-3 seconds.
Slowly straighten the fingers again.
Repeat 10 times. Watch the bend gauge reach the target line.
tips: Move slowly: a smooth, controlled bend scores better than a fast one.

title: Tendon glides
description: A sequence of five hand positions that helps the finger tendons slide smoothly.
steps: Straight hand: fingers straight up, hold 3 s.
Hook fist: bend only the top two joints, knuckles straight, hold 3 s.
Full fist: close the hand completely, thumb over the fingers, hold 3 s.
Tabletop: bend only the big knuckles, fingers straight, hold 3 s.
Straight fist: fingertips touch the base of the palm, hold 3 s.
Return to straight hand. Repeat the sequence 5 times.
tips: Do it in front of the website: the flex reading changes for each position.

title: Hold-and-release bends
description: Builds control and endurance by holding the bend at the target.
steps: Bend the finger until the gauge passes the black target line.
Hold it there for 5 seconds.
Release slowly over 3 seconds until the finger is straight.
Rest 5 seconds.
Repeat 8 times.
tips: If the finger shakes while holding, shorten the hold time and build up gradually.

title: Full-range flexion with blocking
description: Isolates the middle finger joints to reach a complete bend.
steps: Hold the middle finger just below the middle joint with your other hand.
Bend only the top two joints of the middle finger, hold 3 s.
Straighten slowly.
Move your support to just below the top joint and bend only the tip, hold 3 s.
Repeat each 8 times, then do 5 full bends with the glove.
tips: Blocking exercises should never be forced. Ask your therapist before starting if you had tendon surgery.

title: Thumb opposition: touch each fingertip
description: Touch the thumb pad to each fingertip. The thumb touch sensor detects every contact.
steps: Start with the hand open.
Touch the thumb to the tip of the index finger, forming an "O". Hold 2 s.
Open the hand.
Repeat with the middle, ring and little fingers.
Do 3 rounds. In the website, touch when it says "Touch now!".
tips: Try to make a round "O" shape rather than a flat pinch.

title: Quick-response thumb touches
description: Improves speed and coordination between the thumb and fingers.
steps: Rest the hand open on a table.
When the website shows "Touch now!", touch the thumb to the index fingertip as quickly as you can.
Open the hand fully after each touch.
Complete 10 trials and check your average reaction time.
tips: Accuracy first, speed second. A full open-and-touch counts more than a small twitch.

title: Thumb hold and squeeze
description: Strengthens the pinch by holding the thumb contact for longer.
steps: Touch the thumb to the middle fingertip.
Press gently and hold the contact for 5 seconds.
Release and open the hand.
Repeat 8 times, then switch to the index finger.
tips: Keep the pressure gentle. You should feel effort, never pain.
